about.note: The Town of Madison, Carroll County, including Silver Lake and Eidelweiss. Madison is governed by a five-member Board of Selectmen and a Town Administrator, with an annual town meeting: officers and zoning changes are voted by ballot on the second Tuesday in March (March 10, 2026), and money articles at a business session the following Saturday (March 14, 2026). Eidelweiss is also served by the Village District of Eidelweiss, a separate small local government with its own commissioners, water system, roads and tax rate. The town posts Selectmen minutes through September 29, 2026, but those 2026 PDFs could not be opened for this research (only the January 20, 2026 minutes could), so most meeting entries are built from Conway Daily Sun reports and are marked as news reports. The results of the March 14, 2026 business session (including the final operating budget) and the 2025 tax rate breakdown were not found. Plain-English summaries written by AI; items with needs_review=true are uncertain.

issues.title: Investigation into town employees' personal use of town equipment
issues.status: Outside investigator hired in early 2026; money for it was put to the March 2026 town meeting as a separate article. Result of that vote and of the investigation not found.
issues.summary: Residents asked selectmen to stop town employees from using town property and equipment for personal purposes. The board debated whether such use was an accepted perk or against state law, rewrote its personnel policy on town property, and hired an outside firm to investigate. The dispute was part of a contentious spring that saw the board chair change and several staff resign.
points: December 2025: selectmen disagreed over whether employee use of town equipment was a 'perk' (the then-chair and one member) or a violation of state law (Selectman Gray), according to the Daily Sun.

January 20, 2026: the chair said the board was considering Primex, the town's insurer, as a third-party investigator; Town Counsel proposed policy language barring personal use of town property except incidental use.
February 3, 2026: selectmen announced Municipal Resources Inc. would investigate, and that Public Works Director Josh Shackford had resigned.

February 10, 2026 budget hearing: selectmen voted 3-2 (Price, Eldridge and Boewe in favor; Nordlund and Gray against) to move $8,000 for the investigation out of the operating budget into a separate warrant article.
The Daily Sun reported the $8,000 question as Article 24 at the March 14, 2026 business session. The outcome was not found.

issues.title: Replacing the Silver Lake dam
issues.status: Seeking about $2.25 million in federal money; the town is saving in a dam trust fund
issues.next: If federal money comes through, work could start in fall 2027 (Daily Sun, April 2026)
issues.summary: The town owns the roughly 100-year-old dam at the outlet of Silver Lake on East Shore Drive, next to the town boat launch. Selectmen say it is failing and needs replacing; if it failed, the lake could drop 6 to 8 feet. The town has asked U.S. Rep. Chris Pappas for federal funding.
points: Selectmen estimate replacement needs about $2 million. Rep. Pappas's FY2027 Community Project Funding list includes 'Silver Lake Dam Replacement' for the Town of Madison at $2,250,000 (engineering, demolition and a new dam).
Pappas met selectmen at the boat ramp in early April 2026; a staffer said a spending bill with the money could pass at year's end. Not yet awarded.
The 2026 draft warrant (Feb 10 hearing) asked $100,000 for the Silver Lake Dam Improvement Trust Fund, which then held $79,400. Final vote not found.
October 2026: Silver Lake went down to winter level by October 15, then down another 2 feet October 19 to 23 for Public Works repairs to the boat launch (town notice).

issues.title: Eidelweiss and Carroll County dispute over the Oak Ridge emergency radio tower
issues.status: The Village District of Eidelweiss told the county to leave the tower site by December 31, 2026; county commissioners are considering taking the land
issues.next: 2026-12-31: date in the district's eviction notice
issues.summary: Carroll County's emergency communications tower on Oak Ridge in Eidelweiss, used since the 1980s for police, fire and EMS radio across northern Carroll County (including Madison), sits on land owned by the Village District of Eidelweiss. The district says the county has not met its 2017 lease terms, chiefly a $5 million insurance requirement, and sent an eviction notice. This is a district and county matter; the Town of Madison is not a party.
points: August 19, 2026: the district sent the county an eviction notice citing nine years of failing to comply with the 2017 lease. It is not a court order; after December 31 the district may start the formal eviction process.
The county says the $5 million insurance requirement would cost it $10,000 a year and asked the district to lower it and the $400 monthly rent.
Village Commissioner Nancy Cole said the district first sought $6,000 at renewal and agreed to $400 after meeting with the sheriff.
Late October 2026: the Daily Sun reported county commissioners are weighing seizing the land under the tower; Eidelweiss Chair Wooda McNiven called the county's 'stonewalling' claims inaccurate.
Sheriff Dominic Richard said the tower supports police, fire and EMS radio in Conway, Albany, Bartlett, Jackson, Chatham, Tamworth, Freedom and Madison.

issues.title: New selectboard majority, new chair and new Town Administrator
issues.status: Joy Gray chairs the board after the March 2026 election; Lucia Roth hired as Town Administrator in April 2026
issues.summary: In March 2026 voters re-elected Nicole Nordlund and elected Joe Dame, defeating board chair Adam Price. Joy Gray became chair. At an April 14 meeting moved to the elementary school for a crowd of about 75, critics pointed to resignations of an elected official and two employees and to petitions seeking Gray's removal as chair; Selectman Nordlund read a statement defending the board.
points: March 10, 2026: Dame 391 votes, Nordlund 320; challenger Charlie Allen and Chair Adam Price were defeated (their totals were not reported).
Madison voters expanded the board from three to five members in March 2024.

April 14, 2026: Gray announced Lucia Roth, former program manager for New Hampshire's Solar for All program, as Town Administrator and Madison McCarthy as part-time administrative assistant. In January the Town Administrator was Linda Shackford.

Speakers said one elected official and two employees had resigned citing the chair's treatment, and asked why the town treasurer had resigned the week before. The Public Works Director's resignation had been announced in February.
The Planning Board's land use administrator is now Colleen King (in 2025 the role was held by Katharine Young).

issues.status: Planning Board approved the site plan with conditions on December 3, 2025; variances from the Zoning Board still required. Current status not confirmed.
issues.summary: Vertex Towers, LLC proposes a wireless communications facility with a 100-foot monopole at 0 Tasker Hill Road (off Oak Ridge Road, in Eidelweiss). It needs a site plan approval from the Planning Board and four variances (permission to break zoning rules for this one property) from the Zoning Board of Adjustment.
points: ZBA Case 25-06: four variances for the tower; hearing continued from October 15 to November 19, 2025. A balloon test was planned for October 6, 2025.

December 3, 2025: Planning Board Case 25-07 site plan approved 5-0-1 with conditions, including free space for public safety equipment, no tower lighting, a removal bond, weekday 8 AM to 5 PM construction, and protections the Eidelweiss district asked for on its roads and water lines.
The Planning Board page lists a further public hearing on Case PB 25-07 on April 1, 2026; its outcome was not found.
In July 2025 the ZBA unanimously refused to rehear its denial of a different 130-foot tower on King Pine Drive (GMR Holdings).

policy_items.title: Draft 2026 zoning amendments
policy_items.detail: Mostly changes required by new state laws. Accessory dwelling units (a small second home on a lot): the current cap is 800 sq ft; state law sets a 750 sq ft minimum cap; one member proposed 950. The three amendments went on the March 10, 2026 ballot; results not found.
